children: Ethio Telecom expects revenue to jump by 36.7% in the 12 months to June 2027 from the previous period, the state-owned company's chief executive said on Thursday.

Chief Executive Officer, Frehiwot Tamiru, projected the total ​revenue will increase to 295 billion Ethiopian birr  ($1.83 billion), driven by surges in data traffic, customer numbers and network expansion.
The company, which ​the government plans to privatise as part of broader economic liberalisation, held an initial ​public offering (IPO) last year but sold only 10.7% ​of the shares offered.

The firm's total number of subscribers is projected to increase by 6.7% ‌to ⁠96.2 million, while subscribers to its financial service, Telebirr, are seen rising by 11.7% to 68 million, Frehiwot told a press conference.
Ethiopia's telecoms ​industry, serving a ​population of ⁠about 120 million, was considered a big prize when Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed ​took office in 2018 and promised to ​open up ⁠the economy.
It has attracted interest from several foreign companies, including Kenya's Safaricom
, which was part of a consortium ⁠that ​won the country's first private ​telecoms licence in 2021.
